newsitem.title: JAPAN: IAEA chief says N.Korea gives no nuclear details.
newsitem.headline: IAEA chief says N.Korea gives no nuclear details.

text.p: North Korea remained reluctant to provide information on nuclear reactors suspected of being used to produce nuclear weapons, the head of the United Nations' nuclear watchdog said on Wednesday.

Pyongyang refused to give details on how its nuclear reactors had been used and whether nuclear-grade plutonium was extracted from spent nuclear fuel, a Japanese official quoted Hans Blix of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) as saying.
"In regard to the freezing of nuclear facilities, North Korea has been cooperative," the official quoted Blix, IAEA director-general, as saying.
The official said Blix made the remarks in a meeting with Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda.
"But there has been no progress in securing information (on the operations of the nuclear reactors) from North Korea," he was quoted as telling Ikeda.

A crisis over Pyongyang's suspected nuclear weapons programme was defused after North Korea agreed to dismantle its nuclear facilities in return for safer reactors promised by the United States under a landmark accord signed in Geneva in 1994.
The Vienna-based IAEA said in April that North Korea had yet to account for an amount of weapons-grade plutonium that experts say it possesses.
The IAEA has never been able to confirm that the North has a nuclear device but insists it has fissionable material it is not owning up to.
